newsitem.title: GERMANY: GM Europe chiefs unhappy on strategy - report.
newsitem.headline: GM Europe chiefs unhappy on strategy - report.

text.p: Leading European managers at General Motors Corp are dissatisfied with the expansion strategy being pursued by the giant U.S. industrial group, Germany's Der Spiegel magazine reported on Sunday.
Der Spiegel cited an internal GM survey which showed 75 percent of 322 top European managers believed the company was not being run efficiently.

The managers were particularly critical of GM's global strategy, saying that the focus on new factories in South America and Asia was taking away from the success of Adam Opel AG, GM's German plant, the magazine said.
Opel declined comment on the report.
GM intends to use Opel as a base to boost output by about one million units early next century through new plants in such countries as Argentina, Poland, Brazil, Thailand and China.
Opel is helping to develop several of the plants since many will produce Opel vehicles. Opel will turn many of the plants over to GM and receive royalty payments from production.
Industry observers have said the carmaker is focusing too much abroad and has forgotten about its core European strategy.
